text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- First interior ministry report from an investigation into a scandalous crash in which a police chief and a mobster were killed in the same car finds the gangster held seven differrent identity cards.
- Islamist premier Necmettin Erbakan accuses West of delaying Turkey's acceptance into the European Union.
- Washington wants the continuation of a U.S.-led allied airforce stationed in Turkey to protect Iraqi Kurds.
- Turkish bussinessmen and workers go on an investment visit to Greece.
- Justice minister says narcotics squads were not stationed in the southeastern town of Yuksekova because local policemen wanted to get bonuses for seizing drugs themselves.
- The car crash shedding light onto alleged ties between organised crime, the police and the state is being buried in a mountain of words by politicians.
- Ozgorkey company is planning a joint-venture with Coca-Cola.
- It is unclear whether a government MP injured in a car crash in which a top policeman and organised crime boss died will be questioned by the state's security courts.
- Regulations for changing the dress code of civil servants -- so that females can wear the Islamic headscarves and males can grow a beard -- is before ministers for approval.
